name: smart_beta_intraday_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The low-volatility anomaly (low-vol stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns) is documented at monthly horizons but has an intraday analog: stocks in the bottom tercile of realized intraday volatility (measured by 5-day average of intraday high-low range / close) that break out of their compressed range tend to sustain moves because low-vol names attract less noise trading and breakouts are more information-driven. The inefficiency persists because intraday traders prefer high-volatility stocks for larger absolute moves, leaving low-vol breakouts under-exploited. Smart beta indices (NIFTY Low Vol 30) demonstrate this effect at daily frequency; we exploit it at 1-min.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents, bottom tercile by 5-day avg intraday range
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹50 Cr; 5-day average (high-low)/close < median of NIFTY 100

conditions: Stock is in bottom tercile of 5-day avg intraday range (low-vol name)
long.confirmation: Next bar close > Keltner_Upper (breakout holds for 1 bar)

conditions: Stock is in bottom tercile of 5-day avg intraday range

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: 60 bps from entry (low-vol stocks move less, target accordingly)
exit.stop_loss: 30 bps from entry (tight stop — false breakouts in low-vol names are quick)
exit.trailing_stop: After 35 bps profit, trail at 20 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Close re-enters Keltner Channel (close < Keltner_Upper for longs)

risk.position_sizing: Slightly larger size (₹1.25L) due to lower volatility of universe; risk-adjusted via ATR

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22; low-vol breakout strategy works best in calm markets
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 EMA(20) slope > 0 for longs; < 0 for shorts
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 4 bps (tighter for low-vol names)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock 2 days before and after earnings
other_filters: Vol_Percentile must be below 30 (confirming compressed volatility before breakout)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — low-volatility anomaly is persistent and structurally driven by institutional mandates that avoid volatile stocks

weaknesses: Low-vol stocks have smaller absolute moves — 60 bps target is ambitious for names in the bottom tercile of intraday range; many targets may not be hit within time stop
False breakouts in low-vol names often have low volume, making the volume filter critical but also restrictive — may only get 1-2 signals per week
The low-volatility anomaly is documented at monthly frequencies; its persistence at 1-min granularity is unproven and may not hold
prior_art: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011) 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage'; Blitz & van Vliet (2007) low-volatility anomaly; NIFTY Low Volatility 30 index methodology; Keltner Channel breakouts in retail TA
notes: Consider pairing long low-vol breakouts with short high-vol breakdowns for a volatility-neutral portfolio. The strategy naturally has lower turnover and may benefit from slightly longer holding periods.
